target_customer: Pharmaceutical companies and research labs that run protein immunoassays
problem: Protein assays such as ELISA use large sample volumes, manual steps and give end point data, which limits how much biological information pharma can get from small samples.
business_model: Instrument and consumables sales to pharma and life science labs

founders.name: Akwasi Apori
founders.background_notes: Named CEO in the Nov 2020 Series A release. YC page lists him as founder.

founders.name: Kursad Araz
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder and CTO.

founders.name: Samuel Tia
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder. A directory snippet calls him Chief Science Officer; not confirmed on a source I opened.

investors: Regents of the University of California

competitors.name: Quanterix
competitors.what: Ultra sensitive digital immunoassay platform (Simoa) for protein measurement
competitors.traction_then: Aiming for early clinical adoption with high throughput protein assays

technical_complexity.rationale: A protein immobilization method from a Berkeley bioengineering lab turned into a miniaturized, automated immunoassay instrument needs microfluidics, chemistry and hardware development.

defensibility.rationale: University licensed technology gave some IP protection, but adoption depended on beating entrenched ELISA workflows.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. Instrument incumbents kept selling established immunoassay platforms.

market_need_then: Pharma wanted lower sample volumes and faster, richer protein data. By 2020 the company reported pilots with five large pharma companies, per its Series A release.

branding.domain_note: Used correliabio.com (a .com with a bio suffix).
branding.brand_signature: PIXI product name for the automated ELISA platform
branding.community_and_virality: Won the Ignite award for most innovative startup technology at SLAS 2020 per the Series A release.

brand_strength.rationale: Niche B2B science brand with an industry award, but no evidence the name drove adoption.

outcome_analysis: Correlia commercialized a Berkeley microscale protein assay technology, raised a $7 million Series A in November 2020 led by Neotribe Ventures, and launched the PIXI ELISA platform with pharma pilots. The YC directory marks it inactive, yet a database lists a further 2023 round, so the real status and cause of any stall are not public. No failure factors are assigned because no source explains an outcome.
notes: Company site correliabio.com did not resolve in this environment. The 2014 and 2016 grants, the 2018 seed ($0.12M) and the 2023 round of $1.25M (labeled Series A II by CB Insights) rest on a single database. Reported totals raised conflict ($995K to $16.6M) so total is unverified. Quanterix competitor entry is from a 2015 article seen via search snippet only because the fetch was rate limited. Outcome search found no shutdown or acquisition news; cause not public. Founder education and employers not found.
